findings.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:100-117 — DB write of attendees happens before calendar update; if the calendar provider fails, retry is permanently impossible because uniqueGuests filters out already-persisted attendees, causing guests stuck in DB with no invite emails and a desynced calendar event (P2)
addGuests.handler.ts:64-96 — no booking status check; guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending CONFIRMED .ics files that resurrect dead calendar events (P2)

addGuests.handler.ts:87-93 — server-side dedup is case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass via different casing, and does not dedupe duplicates within the guests input array, producing duplicate attendee rows via direct API calls (P2)

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-57 — empty-string entries from MultiEmail initialization and 'add another' button make the multiEmailValue.length === 0 guard dead code and cause valid submissions to be rejected when any empty field remains (P3)
AddGuestsDialog.tsx:66-73 — isInvalidEmail state is never cleared on success, onOpenChange, or re-open; only the Cancel button resets it, so the error banner persists incorrectly (P3)
organizer-add-guests-email.ts:31-34 — renderEmail call omits the teamMember prop that the base organizer-scheduled-email class passes, making per-team-member email rendering dead (P3)
addGuests.handler.ts:158-164 — email-send failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that doesn't even log the error, so the mutation reports success while guests may have received no emails (P3)
addGuests.handler.ts has no dedupe within the submitted guests array and no case normalization, so duplicate attendee rows can be created (uniqueness only enforced client-side)
addGuests.handler.ts permission gate requires user to be both team admin AND team owner, silently excluding team admins who should have access via OR logic
addGuests.handler.ts has no booking status filter, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and receive CONFIRMED calendar invites for dead events
addGuests.handler.ts doesn't handle seated event types (seatsPerTimeSlot), allowing seat capacity to be exceeded and new guests to not be registered as seat holders
No tests shipped for any new behavior, leaving permission matrix, dedupe, blacklist filter, and empty-array rejection unverified
Email failures in addGuests.handler.ts are swallowed with console.log while the API returns success, causing silent notification loss with a success signal to the user
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side while blacklist entries are lowercased, allowing bypass by varying email casing
AddGuestsDialog.tsx isInvalidEmail flag is never cleared on success or edit, so a stale validation error persists when the dialog is reopened
Authorization gate in addGuests.handler.ts:99-101 uses `&&` instead of `||`, so team admins are locked out and only team owners can add guests, despite the UI showing the action to admins

API grants isAttendee mutation rights in addGuests.handler.ts:104-107, allowing any attendee to create unbounded attendee rows, trigger calendar updates against the organizer's event, and send iCal emails to arbitrary addresses, expanding the API surface beyond the organizer-facing UI intent
No booking-status check in addGuests.handler.ts, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, and new attendees receive CONFIRMED iCal REQUESTs for meetings that don't exist

No upper bound on the `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts:4-5, allowing thousands of emails per mutation causing unbounded createMany rows and email fan-out (spam/DoS vector from an authenticated account)

Duplicate and blacklist checks in addGuests.handler.ts:65-73 are case-sensitive while blacklist emails are lowercased, so `User@x.com` bypasses the duplicate check and blacklist, producing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

Seated event types (seatsPerTimeSlot) are not handled in addGuests.handler.ts:150-160: attendees are added via createMany with no capacity check, no seat-record creation, and unaddressed updateCalendarAttendees semantics for seated bookings

Email failure in addGuests.handler.ts:171-174 is swallowed with console.log (discarding the error object) while the API still returns success, so guests are persisted but never notified with no visibility into the failure

addGuests.handler.ts:40-42 — team-permission check uses `&&` where business rule requires `||`: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner requires both roles, but members have exactly one role, so team admins are denied and permission silently degrades to organizer-or-attendee only

addGuests.handler.ts:30-41 — no booking-status guard: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, writing Attendee rows and sending CONFIRMED ics/calendar updates for a meeting that no longer exists

addGuests.schema.ts:4-6 + addGuests.handler.ts:71-77 — TOCTOU duplicate-attendee path: no uniqueness refinement in schema, uniqueGuests only checks stale in-memory snapshot and blacklist, and no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so intra-request or concurrent duplicates create double attendee rows with duplicate email/calendar cycles
addGuests.handler.ts:60-61 — blacklist comparison is case-broken: blacklist emails are lowercased but the guest email is not, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry of 'spam@x.com'

addGuests.handler.ts:157-160 — calendar update runs with the actor's credentials instead of the organizer's: booking.user credentials/destinationCalendar are fetched but EventManager is built from ctx.user, so an attendee adding guests updates the wrong user's calendar

addGuests.handler.ts:106-115 / 158 — non-transactional multi-step write: DB attendee insert commits before calendar update; if updateCalendarAttendees throws (outside try/catch), rows stay committed, error toast says 'unable_to_add_guests', and cache/UI state diverges from DB

addGuests.handler.ts:163-168 — email failure swallowed as console.log with error object discarded: total email provider failure produces no log body, no metric, no retry, user still gets success message, and Promise.all fanout discards batch error details

addGuests.schema.ts:6 — unbounded guests array with no max() cap: a single authenticated request can trigger thousands of outbound emails and calendar API calls via createMany, sendAddGuestsEmails, and updateCalendarAttendees (amplification path)

addGuests.handler.ts:36-49 — seated-event capacity invariant not enforced: seatsPerTimeSlot is read but never checked against existing attendees + new guests, and bare Attendee rows bypass the seat machinery, allowing over-capacity guests

email-manager.ts:538-542 — O(n·m) array membership scan (newGuests.includes) should use a Set; also newGuests is raw client input vs stored attendee.email so casing divergence makes new guests receive the wrong email template
Authorization gate in addGuests.handler.ts:57-59 uses && instead of ||, narrowing 'team admin or owner' to 'team owner only', so team admins who aren't owners get FORBIDDEN errors

No booking.status guard in addGuests.handler.ts:33-67; guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, and attendee-add-guests-email.ts:14 hardcodes status CONFIRMED with method REQUEST, sending a CONFIRMED iCalendar REQUEST that resurrects cancelled meetings in calendars

isAttendee branch in addGuests.handler.ts:61-67 grants any booking attendee permission to add arbitrary guests via API, exceeding the permission model the UI encodes (UI exposes the action only to booking owner/team)

Email uniqueness is only enforced client-side; addGuests.schema.ts uses z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine, and the handler's dedupe only removes guests already on the booking, so direct API calls with duplicate emails create duplicate Attendee rows and send duplicate invites

Blacklisted guests are filtered out silently in addGuests.handler.ts:82-89 and the mutation always returns success, so the client shows 'Guests added' even when requested guests were dropped with no feedback about rejected emails

Calendar attendee update in addGuests.handler.ts:155-158 runs with the acting user's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees may silently fail while ICS emails still go out, diverging email and calendar state

Booking lookup in addGuests.handler.ts:38 is unscoped (`WHERE id = bookingId` with no user/org filter), and the post-hoc attendee-match authz allows any registered user who is or can be listed as an attendee to mutate any booking, add arbitrary recipients, and trigger calendar/email fan-out

Attendee emails are user-supplied and unverified, so attackers can add arbitrary email addresses to a private event, causing those addresses to receive the full event ICS including title, description, location, and video-call meetingUrl/meetingPassword (disclosure of private meeting join links)
No cap on `guests` array length and no rate limiting, allowing a single participant to email-bomb arbitrary addresses via repeated calls

Authorization compound at addGuests.handler.ts:33-35 uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, requiring the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously — an inverted/dead check that always evaluates false for team bookings, causing silent fall-through to organizer/attendee checks
If `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null, `?? 0` queries team 0 in the team authorization checks

Guest blacklist comparison is case-mismatched: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guests` is compared verbatim, trivially bypassing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS via case variation (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` vs `blocked@example.com`)
Existing-attendee dedupe comparison is also case-mismatched (`guest === attendee.email`), so case-varied emails create duplicate attendee rows

Server schema `addGuests.schema.ts` (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) enforces neither uniqueness nor max length; uniqueness refinement only exists in the client dialog, so direct tRPC calls can send unlimited duplicate entries

Email-send failure at addGuests.handler.ts:162-166 is swallowed with a message-free log (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, err discarded) while the handler returns "Guests added" success, hiding failures where victims never receive notification that unknown parties were appended to their event

addGuests.handler.ts:47-49 uses && operator for isTeamAdminOrOwner instead of ||, so non-owner team admins are incorrectly denied permission to add guests despite the variable name and UI promising admin access

addGuests.handler.ts:170-173 catches errors from sendAddGuestsEmails and only logs them, returning success unconditionally so clients believe guests were added even when all notification emails and ICS updates failed

Client-side AddGuestsDialog schema enforces email uniqueness via .refine but the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) has no uniqueness check, allowing duplicate emails to reach createMany and cause a Prisma unique-constraint rejection or duplicate rows when called by non-React clients

email-manager.ts:525-549 compares raw user-input newGuests against attendee emails case-sensitively, so newly added guests with case-variant addresses receive the wrong email template (notification for existing attendees instead of their own confirmation)

BookingListItem.tsx:193-200 adds the add_members action unconditionally for all booking states and reuses data-testid="add_members" for both the menu item and dialog submit button, making E2E selectors ambiguous between opening the dialog and submitting it

No test files in the diff cover the new addGuests permission branch, error handling, duplicate-guest handling, email fan-out fork, or new email templates (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, OrganizerAddGuestsEmail)

addGuests.handler.ts:100-109 — attendee insert via prisma.booking.update is committed without a transaction; if the subsequent updateCalendarAttendees call throws, DB rows are committed but never pushed to the calendar, and the retry path is broken because uniqueGuests then filters out all guests causing BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', leaving an unreconcilable inconsistency

addGuests.handler.ts:169-173 — calendar/email failure is swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), so guests exist in DB and calendar but never receive the ICS REQUEST notification, silently with no detection or repair

addGuests.handler.ts:65-72 — duplicate-attendee dedupe is case-sensitive (exact string match) and ZAddGuestsInputSchema doesn't enforce uniqueness within guests, with no @@unique([bookingId, email]) DB constraint, so duplicate Attendee rows for the same person can be created via direct tRPC calls or differing email casing

addGuests.handler.ts:65-67 — BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS silently drops blacklisted guests with no error or feedback; the caller receives 'Guests added' success and cannot tell some submitted guests were discarded

addGuests.handler.ts:27-40 + 100-109 — the dedupe/blacklist check runs against a stale pre-fetch booking.attendees snapshot, so two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking both pass the filter and both createMany the same guest, producing duplicates with no unique constraint to catch it

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:100-117 — DB write of attendees happens before calendar update; if the calendar provider fails, retry is permanently impossible because uniqueGuests filters out already-persisted attendees, causing guests stuck in DB with no invite emails and a desynced calendar event (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code persists new attendees first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...) and only afterwards calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g., calendar provider/API failure), the mutation fails after the DB has already been updated, leaving attendees added in DB but no calendar update performed. On a later retry with the same guest emails, uniqueGuests is computed by filtering out emails already in booking.attendees, so it will become empty and the handler throws BAD_REQUEST, preventing retry/reconciliation via this endpoint. This matches the finding’s desync/permanent-retry issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:64-96 — no booking status check; guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending CONFIRMED .ics files that resurrect dead calendar events (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking by `id` only and proceeds to `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` without checking any booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected). The newly added email templates always generate an `.ics` with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`), so invoking this mutation on a non-active booking would send “confirmed” calendar updates/emails, which is inconsistent and can effectively resurrect cancelled events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:87-93 — server-side dedup is case-sensitive, allowing blacklist bypass via different casing, and does not dedupe duplicates within the guests input array, producing duplicate attendee rows via direct API calls (P2)

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-57 — empty-string entries from MultiEmail initialization and 'add another' button make the multiEmailValue.length === 0 guard dead code and cause valid submissions to be rejected when any empty field remains (P3)
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same root problem: initializing MultiEmail state with an empty string (and allowing additional empty entries) leads to validation/guard logic behaving incorrectly and can reject otherwise valid submissions. The golden suggests starting with [] and handling empty state; the candidate describes the resulting dead-code guard and rejection due to empty fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:66-73 — isInvalidEmail state is never cleared on success, onOpenChange, or re-open; only the Cancel button resets it, so the error banner persists incorrectly (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd`), but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler. The success path (`addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`) closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not clear `isInvalidEmail`. Since the dialog component stays mounted in `BookingListItem` and `onOpenChange` only toggles `isOpenDialog` without resetting the flag, the error banner can persist after closing/reopening or even after a successful add.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts:31-34 — renderEmail call omits the teamMember prop that the base organizer-scheduled-email class passes, making per-team-member email rendering dead (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the `renderEmail("OrganizerAddGuestsEmail", { ... })` payload only includes `{ attendee: this.calEvent.organizer, calEvent: this.calEvent }` and does not include `teamMember`, even though `sendAddGuestsEmails` constructs `new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent, teamMember })` for each team member and the class uses `this.teamMember` for addressing. This means the React/template render layer cannot vary content based on `teamMember` from the data provided here. However, the diff does not show the base `OrganizerScheduledEmail`/template requirements, so the claim that per-team-member rendering is fully "dead" is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158-164 — email-send failure is swallowed with a bare console.log that doesn't even log the error, so the mutation reports success while guests may have received no emails (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler then returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`) regardless. This does mean email failures are swallowed and not even logged with the actual `err`, but the core mutation behavior (adding attendees + updating calendar) has already happened and is not shown to depend on email delivery, so it’s not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone—more an observability/UX/error-reporting concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts has no dedupe within the submitted guests array and no case normalization, so duplicate attendee rows can be created (uniqueness only enforced client-side)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness check, and the handler builds `uniqueGuests` via `guests.filter(...)` only against existing `booking.attendees` and blacklist—there is no dedupe of duplicates within the submitted `guests` array. It also compares emails case-sensitively (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not lowercase/normalize, so `A@x.com` vs `a@x.com` can bypass checks. As a result, `createMany` can create duplicate attendee rows for the same booking unless the DB enforces uniqueness (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts permission gate requires user to be both team admin AND team owner, silently excluding team admins who should have access via OR logic
addGuests.handler.ts has no booking status filter, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and receive CONFIRMED calendar invites for dead events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched only by `id` (no `status`/cancellation check) and then updated (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and calendar/email notifications are sent. The new email templates generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts` / `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). If a cancelled/rejected booking can still be fetched by id, this handler would still add attendees and send CONFIRMED invites for an event that may no longer be valid, which is incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts doesn't handle seated event types (seatsPerTimeSlot), allowing seat capacity to be exceeded and new guests to not be registered as seat holders

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (which is present on the booking’s event type and is passed into the `CalendarEvent`). This means for seated/limited-capacity event types, the code can add more guests than the seat limit, effectively exceeding capacity. The diff also shows no additional persistence/update of any seat-specific structure beyond `attendees`, so there is no visible mechanism here to enforce or record seat allocation when seats are enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests shipped for any new behavior, leaving permission matrix, dedupe, blacklist filter, and empty-array rejection unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (new TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests`, permission gating in `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklist filtering via `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, dedupe/uniqueness handling in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` and server-side filtering, and an explicit rejection when no new guests remain). No test files or test changes are present in the diff to verify this new permission matrix and edge cases (dedupe/blacklist/empty resulting array).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failures in addGuests.handler.ts are swallowed with console.log while the API returns success, causing silent notification loss with a success signal to the user

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. This means email/notification delivery can fail silently while the client mutation resolves successfully (and the UI shows a success toast in `AddGuestsDialog`), matching the finding of silent notification loss with a success signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side while blacklist entries are lowercased, allowing bypass by varying email casing
AddGuestsDialog.tsx isInvalidEmail flag is never cleared on success or edit, so a stale validation error persists when the dialog is reopened

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but it is not reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler (which only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Since the dialog component remains mounted (toggled via `isOpenDialog`), reopening the dialog after a previous validation failure can show the stale error message (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) even after success/close. It’s only cleared on Cancel (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`), and not on edit of the emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization gate in addGuests.handler.ts:99-101 uses `&&` instead of `||`, so team admins are locked out and only team owners can add guests, despite the UI showing the action to admins
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same permission-check bug: the code uses AND (&&) requiring a user to be both team admin and team owner, but it should be OR (||) so either role grants access. Candidate adds impact details (admins locked out).

adjudication_records.issue_text: API grants isAttendee mutation rights in addGuests.handler.ts:104-107, allowing any attendee to create unbounded attendee rows, trigger calendar updates against the organizer's event, and send iCal emails to arbitrary addresses, expanding the API surface beyond the organizer-facing UI intent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to call the mutation: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard only forbids when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` (so `isAttendee` passes). The handler then performs side effects on the organizer’s booking: it `booking.update` creates new attendee rows via `createMany`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (updating calendar attendees for the event), and sends emails via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` to the provided addresses. There is no diff-shown limit on `guests` array size, so an attendee can add arbitrary numbers of guests and trigger calendar/email side effects, matching the finding’s concern about expanded API surface beyond organizer-only intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status check in addGuests.handler.ts, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, and new attendees receive CONFIRMED iCal REQUESTs for meetings that don't exist

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking and then proceeds to (1) create new attendee records, (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) send ICS emails whose payload hard-codes `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. There is no conditional logic anywhere in the added handler that checks any booking lifecycle/status (e.g., cancelled/rejected/pending) before allowing guest addition or before sending CONFIRMED requests. If such non-confirmed/cancelled states exist (common for bookings), this would result in incorrect behavior consistent with the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound on the `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts:4-5, allowing thousands of emails per mutation causing unbounded createMany rows and email fan-out (spam/DoS vector from an authenticated account)

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or any other bound). The handler then uses `createMany` to insert all `uniqueGuests` (`addGuests.handler.ts`), and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which fans out emails across attendees/team members. From the diff alone, an authenticated caller can submit a very large `guests` array, leading to unbounded DB writes and email sending (DoS/spam risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate and blacklist checks in addGuests.handler.ts:65-73 are case-sensitive while blacklist emails are lowercased, so `User@x.com` bypasses the duplicate check and blacklist, producing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the filtering for `uniqueGuests` is case-sensitive: it checks `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (lines around the shown `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). However `blacklistedGuestEmails` are explicitly lowercased, while `guest` is not normalized. Therefore an input like `User@x.com` can bypass both the existing-attendee duplicate check (if stored as `user@x.com`) and the blacklist check, leading to duplicate attendee rows/emails differing only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seated event types (seatsPerTimeSlot) are not handled in addGuests.handler.ts:150-160: attendees are added via createMany with no capacity check, no seat-record creation, and unaddressed updateCalendarAttendees semantics for seated bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (seated capacity) and without creating/updating any seat-specific records (none referenced in this handler). Yet the emitted `CalendarEvent` includes `seatsPerTimeSlot` / `seatsShowAttendees` and the handler calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, implying seated semantics may matter. This makes it possible (from what the diff shows) to add guests beyond seat capacity and/or leave seated booking state inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure in addGuests.handler.ts:171-174 is swallowed with console.log (discarding the error object) while the API still returns success, so guests are persisted but never notified with no visibility into the failure

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try/catch` and on failure it only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (discarding `err`) and then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. This means the mutation can succeed (guests persisted + calendar updated) while notifications silently fail with no actionable visibility into the error, despite this diff explicitly adding the guest-added email notification feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:40-42 — team-permission check uses `&&` where business rule requires `||`: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner requires both roles, but members have exactly one role, so team admins are denied and permission silently degrades to organizer-or-attendee only

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the permission flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` but is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and is then used to gate access (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). With `&&`, a user who is a team admin but not a team owner will fail this check and be denied unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee, which is likely unintended for a team-level operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:30-41 — no booking-status guard: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, writing Attendee rows and sending CONFIRMED ics/calendar updates for a meeting that no longer exists

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched only by `id` (no `where` condition on any booking status) and the handler proceeds to (1) write new attendee rows via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, (2) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) send emails whose ICS payloads are explicitly marked `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. The diff shows no guard preventing this flow for cancelled/rejected/pending bookings, so guests could be added and CONFIRMED calendar updates sent even if the booking should no longer be active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:4-6 + addGuests.handler.ts:71-77 — TOCTOU duplicate-attendee path: no uniqueness refinement in schema, uniqueGuests only checks stale in-memory snapshot and blacklist, and no DB unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so intra-request or concurrent duplicates create double attendee rows with duplicate email/calendar cycles

adjudication.rationale: Server-side validation in `addGuests.schema.ts` only enforces `email()` (no uniqueness), and `addGuests.handler.ts` computes `uniqueGuests` only by comparing against the initially fetched `booking.attendees` and a blacklist, not by deduping the `guests` array itself. It then calls `attendees.createMany` with `guestsFullDetails`, so duplicate emails in the input (or duplicates added since the initial read) can result in duplicate attendee rows unless a DB unique constraint exists (not shown in this diff). The client adds a uniqueness refine in `AddGuestsDialog`, but that can be bypassed via direct API calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:60-61 — blacklist comparison is case-broken: blacklist emails are lowercased but the guest email is not, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry of 'spam@x.com'

addGuests.handler.ts:157-160 — calendar update runs with the actor's credentials instead of the organizer's: booking.user credentials/destinationCalendar are fetched but EventManager is built from ctx.user, so an attendee adding guests updates the wrong user's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is loaded with `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`, but those organizer-specific fields are never used. Instead, the calendar update path builds `EventManager` from the actor (`ctx.user`) and calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then runs `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If an attendee (allowed by `isAttendee`) adds guests, this will use the attendee’s credentials rather than the organizer/booking owner’s, which can update the wrong user’s connected calendar or fail to update the organizer’s calendar at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:106-115 / 158 — non-transactional multi-step write: DB attendee insert commits before calendar update; if updateCalendarAttendees throws (outside try/catch), rows stay committed, error toast says 'unable_to_add_guests', and cache/UI state diverges from DB

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding try/catch or DB transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation fails but the attendee rows have already been committed, leaving DB state changed while the client sees an error and may not invalidate/refetch (invalidation happens only in `onSuccess`). This is a real multi-step consistency bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:163-168 — email failure swallowed as console.log with error object discarded: total email provider failure produces no log body, no metric, no retry, user still gets success message, and Promise.all fanout discards batch error details

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. The catch discards `err` (no stack/context), so a provider outage would yield only a generic log line with no actionable error details; there’s also no propagation/metric/retry behavior shown. This is a concrete robustness/observability issue grounded in the diff, but the core mutation (DB update + calendar attendee update) still succeeds, so it’s not a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:6 — unbounded guests array with no max() cap: a single authenticated request can trigger thousands of outbound emails and calendar API calls via createMany, sendAddGuestsEmails, and updateCalendarAttendees (amplification path)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authed mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` whose input schema (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` bound. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) then (1) `createMany` inserts all provided guests, (2) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with the expanded attendee list, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which builds `emailsToSend` over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends them all. This creates a clear amplification/abuse path from a single authenticated request to potentially massive DB writes + outbound email/calendar updates, with no limiting shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:36-49 — seated-event capacity invariant not enforced: seatsPerTimeSlot is read but never checked against existing attendees + new guests, and bare Attendee rows bypass the seat machinery, allowing over-capacity guests

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, guests are added via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any capacity check. Although `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` is read and propagated into the `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), the handler never compares `(existing attendees + uniqueGuests)` against `seatsPerTimeSlot` before inserting new attendee rows. This means for seated/capacity-limited events, the endpoint can overbook by adding extra attendees, bypassing any seat-limit invariant that would otherwise be enforced at the booking/seats layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:538-542 — O(n·m) array membership scan (newGuests.includes) should use a Set; also newGuests is raw client input vs stored attendee.email so casing divergence makes new guests receive the wrong email template

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters to `uniqueGuests` before creating new attendee records, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw client input `guests` (not `uniqueGuests`). In `email-manager.ts` `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the template selection depends on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. Because `newGuests` is the unfiltered input, existing attendees that were re-submitted (or blacklisted/filtered out) can be incorrectly treated as “new” and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` again. Also, `includes` is case-sensitive and the diff shows no normalization (neither in schema nor before comparison), so casing differences between stored `attendee.email` and input can cause new guests to be misclassified and receive the wrong email template. The Set/perf note is secondary, but the misclassification is a real behavior defect grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization gate in addGuests.handler.ts:57-59 uses && instead of ||, narrowing 'team admin or owner' to 'team owner only', so team admins who aren't owners get FORBIDDEN errors

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` (lines shown around 57-59), which requires the user to be both a team admin and the team owner. The variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and the subsequent gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` indicate it was meant to allow either role; as written, team admins who are not owners will be incorrectly forbidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking.status guard in addGuests.handler.ts:33-67; guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, and attendee-add-guests-email.ts:14 hardcodes status CONFIRMED with method REQUEST, sending a CONFIRMED iCalendar REQUEST that resurrects cancelled meetings in calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking and performs permission checks, but never checks `booking.status` (or any cancellation/rejection flag) before updating attendees and syncing calendars (`prisma.booking.update(...)` then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`). That means guests can be added and calendar updates/emails sent even for bookings that may be CANCELLED/REJECTED. Separately, the new email templates `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `.../organizer-add-guests-email.ts` generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` unconditionally; if invoked for a cancelled booking this would send a CONFIRMED REQUEST update, which can plausibly re-add/reconfirm an event in recipients’ calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAttendee branch in addGuests.handler.ts:61-67 grants any booking attendee permission to add arbitrary guests via API, exceeding the permission model the UI encodes (UI exposes the action only to booking owner/team)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the forbidden check is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`. This means any user who is an attendee on the booking can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests` and mutate the booking’s attendees list via API, which is a meaningful permission escalation unless explicitly intended. The diff does not show server-side constraints limiting this action to organizer/team only, so the finding (attendees can add arbitrary guests) is verifiably true from the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email uniqueness is only enforced client-side; addGuests.schema.ts uses z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine, and the handler's dedupe only removes guests already on the booking, so direct API calls with duplicate emails create duplicate Attendee rows and send duplicate invites
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that the server-side logic only filters out existing/blacklisted attendees but does not deduplicate duplicate emails within the incoming request, allowing createMany to insert duplicate Attendee rows (and potentially send duplicate invites).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted guests are filtered out silently in addGuests.handler.ts:82-89 and the mutation always returns success, so the client shows 'Guests added' even when requested guests were dropped with no feedback about rejected emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that are already attendees and any in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (lines ~82-89). The handler only errors when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`; otherwise it proceeds to create attendees for the remaining emails and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. The client dialog always shows a generic success toast (`t("guests_added")`) on mutation success, with no indication that some requested emails may have been dropped. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/feedback gap (potentially intentional for blacklist privacy), but not necessarily a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar attendee update in addGuests.handler.ts:155-158 runs with the acting user's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees may silently fail while ICS emails still go out, diverging email and calendar state

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler authorizes not only the organizer but also team admin/owner and even an attendee (`isAttendee`). However, it builds the `EventManager` using the acting session user (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`) rather than the booking organizer (`booking.user` is fetched with `credentials` but never used). If a non-organizer triggers `addGuests`, `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update calendars using the wrong user's credentials, potentially failing to update the organizer’s/booking’s connected calendar while the DB attendees are updated and emails are still attempted, causing calendar/email/DB state divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking lookup in addGuests.handler.ts:38 is unscoped (`WHERE id = bookingId` with no user/org filter), and the post-hoc attendee-match authz allows any registered user who is or can be listed as an attendee to mutate any booking, add arbitrary recipients, and trigger calendar/email fan-out

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched solely by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and authorization is applied afterwards. The authz explicitly allows any existing attendee to proceed (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). That means any attendee of a booking (not just the organizer/admin) can call this mutation to `booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`, causing calendar updates and email fan-out to arbitrary addresses. This is a concrete, diff-grounded privilege issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee emails are user-supplied and unverified, so attackers can add arbitrary email addresses to a private event, causing those addresses to receive the full event ICS including title, description, location, and video-call meetingUrl/meetingPassword (disclosure of private meeting join links)

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` feature allows a logged-in user who is merely an existing attendee (`isAttendee` check in `addGuests.handler.ts`) to add arbitrary email addresses (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) with no ownership/verification beyond format and a blacklist. The handler persists them as booking attendees (`booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), updates calendar attendees, and then sends emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) where the `CalendarEvent` `evt` includes sensitive fields like `location` and potentially `videoCallData` (`meetingUrl`/`meetingPassword`). Thus, an attendee can cause full event/ICS content to be sent to arbitrary third-party addresses, which is a privacy/security disclosure as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on `guests` array length and no rate limiting, allowing a single participant to email-bomb arbitrary addresses via repeated calls

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` or other bound (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`), and the handler will create attendees and then send emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) for the provided list (`addGuests.handler.ts`). The UI (`MultiEmail`) also allows adding an arbitrary number of email inputs. No throttling/rate-limiting or per-request cap is shown in the diff, so this change introduces an abuse vector where an authorized caller (even an attendee is permitted by the handler) can trigger large volumes of outbound email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization compound at addGuests.handler.ts:33-35 uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, requiring the user to be both admin and owner simultaneously — an inverted/dead check that always evaluates false for team bookings, causing silent fall-through to organizer/attendee checks

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Given the variable name and typical authorization intent, this likely should be an OR check (admin OR owner). As written, a team admin who is not also the owner (or vice versa) will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and can be incorrectly denied unless they also happen to be the booking organizer or an attendee, leading to unintended FORBIDDEN for legitimate team roles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null, `?? 0` queries team 0 in the team authorization checks

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the team authorization uses `(booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)` in calls to `isTeamAdmin` / `isTeamOwner`. If `teamId` is null/undefined (e.g., a non-team event), this will run the checks against team id `0`, which is not the booking’s team and could incorrectly grant authorization if a team with id 0 exists or those helpers treat 0 specially. This behavior is introduced by the new handler in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guest blacklist comparison is case-mismatched: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guests` is compared verbatim, trivially bypassing BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS via case variation (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` vs `blocked@example.com`)
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: the blacklist is lowercased but the incoming guest emails are not, so case variations can bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS when using includes() for comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedupe comparison is also case-mismatched (`guest === attendee.email`), so case-varied emails create duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe check is `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` which is case-sensitive. Since inputs are only validated as emails (no normalization to lowercase) and existing attendee emails may differ in casing, adding `Test@x.com` when `test@x.com` already exists would bypass the check and create a duplicate attendee row via `createMany`. The dialog-side uniqueness check also uses a case-sensitive `Set`, reinforcing the issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema `addGuests.schema.ts` (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) enforces neither uniqueness nor max length; uniqueness refinement only exists in the client dialog, so direct tRPC calls can send unlimited duplicate entries

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness or size bound. The client dialog adds a uniqueness refine, but that can be bypassed via direct tRPC calls. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters against existing booking attendees and a blacklist, but does not dedupe within the provided `guests` array, so duplicate emails in the input can still flow into `createMany` and/or cause unintended duplicate attendee records or errors. There is also no max-length protection against very large arrays.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send failure at addGuests.handler.ts:162-166 is swallowed with a message-free log (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`, err discarded) while the handler returns "Guests added" success, hiding failures where victims never receive notification that unknown parties were appended to their event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after successfully mutating attendees and updating calendars, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and discards `err`, then the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`). This means the client/UI will show success (`showToast(t("guests_added"))`) even when the notification side-effect fails, and the failure is effectively hidden with no error details logged from the caught exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:47-49 uses && operator for isTeamAdminOrOwner instead of ||, so non-owner team admins are incorrectly denied permission to add guests despite the variable name and UI promising admin access

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both an admin and an owner. Given the variable name (`AdminOrOwner`) and the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this will incorrectly forbid non-owner team admins from adding guests. Using `||` (or a different role check) is likely intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:170-173 catches errors from sendAddGuestsEmails and only logs them, returning success unconditionally so clients believe guests were added even when all notification emails and ICS updates failed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler performs the core mutation (DB `booking.update` adding attendees) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` outside the `try/catch`, so an ICS/calendar update failure would still throw and not return success. However, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s on failure and then continues to `return { message: "Guests added" }`, meaning the client will see success even if all notification emails fail. That’s a real, diff-grounded concern, but it’s about error reporting/observability of a secondary side-effect rather than a verified functional defect in adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side AddGuestsDialog schema enforces email uniqueness via .refine but the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) has no uniqueness check, allowing duplicate emails to reach createMany and cause a Prisma unique-constraint rejection or duplicate rows when called by non-React clients

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the client validates uniqueness via `z.array(...).refine(...)`, but the server input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` only checks `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees/blacklist but does not dedupe duplicates within `guests`, and then `createMany` is called with `guestsFullDetails` built from that list (no `skipDuplicates`). This allows a non-React client to send duplicate emails and potentially create duplicate attendee rows or trigger a DB uniqueness error if such a constraint exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts:525-549 compares raw user-input newGuests against attendee emails case-sensitively, so newly added guests with case-variant addresses receive the wrong email template (notification for existing attendees instead of their own confirmation)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` the new `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` checks `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. `newGuests` originates from the TRPC input (`addGuests.schema.ts` uses `z.string().email()` with no normalization), and the handler passes the raw `guests` array into `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` without lowercasing. Because `Array.includes` is case-sensitive, a newly added guest whose email casing differs from the stored attendee email casing will not match and will receive the wrong template. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BookingListItem.tsx:193-200 adds the add_members action unconditionally for all booking states and reuses data-testid="add_members" for both the menu item and dialog submit button, making E2E selectors ambiguous between opening the dialog and submitting it

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test files in the diff cover the new addGuests permission branch, error handling, duplicate-guest handling, email fan-out fork, or new email templates (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, OrganizerAddGuestsEmail)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new logic (viewer.bookings.addGuests TRPC route + addGuestsHandler permission checks, blacklist/duplicate filtering and BAD_REQUEST branch, calendar attendee update, and email fan-out in sendAddGuestsEmails plus new templates AttendeeAddGuestsEmail/OrganizerAddGuestsEmail). adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:100-109 — attendee insert via prisma.booking.update is committed without a transaction; if the subsequent updateCalendarAttendees call throws, DB rows are committed but never pushed to the calendar, and the retry path is broken because uniqueGuests then filters out all guests causing BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', leaving an unreconcilable inconsistency

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB write happens first via prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) and is not wrapped in a transaction. Immediately after, the code awaits eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) with no try/catch. If that call throws, the function aborts after the DB commit, leaving attendees persisted but calendar attendees not updated. On retry, the handler re-reads booking.attendees and computes uniqueGuests by filtering out already-present attendees, so the same input will likely yield uniqueGuests.length === 0 and throw BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid", preventing reconciliation. This inconsistent, unrecoverable state is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:169-173 — calendar/email failure is swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), so guests exist in DB and calendar but never receive the ICS REQUEST notification, silently with no detection or repair

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB is updated (`prisma.booking.update(...)`) and calendars are updated (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`) before attempting to notify via email. The email send is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch { console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'); }`, which swallows any failure and still returns success (`return { message: 'Guests added' }`). Since the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `email()` and `createMany` inserts all `guestsFullDetails`, a direct tRPC call can create duplicate attendee rows (e.g., repeated emails in `guests`, or casing variants vs existing `attendee.email`). adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the server builds `blacklistedGuestEmails` and then filters submitted `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by excluding already-attending and blacklisted emails. If some submitted emails are blacklisted (but at least one isn’t), the mutation proceeds, updates attendees only with `uniqueGuests`, and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` with no indication that some inputs were ignored. That matches the finding: partial drops are silent unless *all* submitted guests are filtered out (then it throws BAD_REQUEST). This is a real diff-grounded behavior/UX/API contract concern rather than a provable correctness failure given blacklist may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:27-40 + 100-109 — the dedupe/blacklist check runs against a stale pre-fetch booking.attendees snapshot, so two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking both pass the filter and both createMany the same guest, producing duplicates with no unique constraint to catch it

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against the initially fetched `booking.attendees` (pre-update snapshot), then performs `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with those emails. The diff shows no transactional re-check (e.g., conditional insert / upsert / unique constraint handling) around the insert, so two concurrent `addGuests` mutations for the same `bookingId` can both pass the prefilter and both `createMany` the same guest email, resulting in duplicates or an insertion race.
